EPIC Sports Complex — McComb, MS
EPIC Life Academy · 501(c)(3)

THE ACADEMY

Athletics are the vehicle. The destination is a young person who is okay.

Why It Exists

THE PART THAT ISN'T ABOUT SPORTS

EPIC Life Academy is the non-profit that runs alongside the building. It exists because the hardest things young people in this region carry — anxiety, grief, pressure at home, the feeling that there is nowhere to go after the last bell — do not stop at the gym door. They walk in with the kid.

A sports facility can pretend that isn't happening and just sell court time. We decided not to. The Academy delivers youth development and mental wellness programming inside the complex from the day it opens, funded separately from the facility so it never competes with a rental for priority.

Sport is what gets a young person through the door. Showing up three times a week to something that expects you, with adults who notice when you are off, is what does the work.

Architectural concept rendering — facility in development
Mental Wellness

WHAT WE ACTUALLY DO

We are careful about this, because youth mental health is a place where good intentions can do harm. Here is exactly what the Academy is and is not.

MENTAL PERFORMANCE CURRICULUM

A season-long, age-banded curriculum taught in the gym rather than a classroom: managing pressure, self-talk, setting goals you control, recovering from a bad game, and what to do with the feeling after a loss. Built for how a twelve-year-old actually talks.

EVERY ADULT TRAINED

Coaches, front-desk staff and event workers complete Youth Mental Health First Aid and mandated reporter training before they work a shift. The person running the drill should be able to recognise a young person who is struggling and know the next step.

A REAL REFERRAL PATH

When a young person needs more than a coach can give, the family gets a warm handoff to licensed providers in the region — a name, a call made with them, a follow-up. Not a pamphlet on the way out.

FAMILY PROGRAMMING

Free evening sessions for parents and guardians on what teenage anxiety and depression look like from the outside, how to start a conversation that doesn't shut down, and where help exists locally.

PEER LEADERSHIP COUNCIL

Older athletes trained to look out for younger ones. Being responsible for somebody else is one of the most protective things a struggling teenager can have, and it is the part of this that kids ask for.

QUIET SPACE

A low-stimulation room off the main floor for an athlete who needs ten minutes away from the noise. No explanation required to use it. Small, and it matters more than it sounds.

What the Academy is not. EPIC Life Academy is not a clinic. We do not diagnose, we do not provide therapy or counselling, and we do not prescribe. Our staff are trained to notice, to respond appropriately, and to connect families with licensed professionals who do that work. Anything else would be dishonest and unsafe, and we would rather say so plainly on our own website.

Youth Programs

WHAT A KID CAN ACTUALLY DO HERE

Programming runs year-round across both sides of the building, priced for Pike County and open to every young person in the trade area regardless of ability, experience or family income.

Ages 5–14

YOUTH COMMUNITY LEAGUES

In-house recreational basketball, volleyball and flag football. Everybody plays. The point is a season with a team, a coach who learns your name, and a schedule you can count on — not a travel roster.

Ages 8–18

SKILLS ACADEMIES

Position-specific training across basketball, volleyball, soccer and diamond sports, including the Alijah Martin Basketball Academy. Small groups, real coaching, no year-round travel commitment required.

Ages 10–18

SPEED & DEVELOPMENT

Strength, speed, agility and injury-prevention work on the turf, taught the way it should be at this age — movement quality first, load second, with coaches who understand growing bodies.

All ages

ADAPTIVE & INCLUSIVE PLAY

Sessions built for young people with physical and developmental disabilities, on the same floors as everyone else. Families in this region drive a long way for this. They shouldn't have to.

Ages 11–18

STUDY HALL & ACADEMIC SUPPORT

Supervised homework hours before evening training, with tutoring in partnership with area schools. Eligibility support for athletes who need their grades to keep playing.

Ages 14–18

LIFE AFTER THE BUZZER

Financial literacy, first-job readiness, college and career pathways, and recruiting reality for the ninety-nine percent who will not play professionally. Taught by people who have been through it.

Access

NOBODY PRICED OUT

Pike County's median household income sits well below the state average. A facility that ignores that is a facility for somebody else's community.

  • Memberships start at $20 a month — built for this market, not imported from a metro.
  • A scholarship fund covers league registration, camp fees and equipment for families who need it. Applications are simple, confidential, and reviewed by the Academy board rather than facility staff.
  • School and church group rates for organised youth programming.
  • Free community open-gym hours each week, funded by sponsors.
  • Transportation partnerships with area schools and churches, because a program a child cannot get to is not a program.

Safeguarding

HOW WE KEEP KIDS SAFE

Youth safety is a design decision, not a policy document. It is built into how the building works.

  • Background checks and reference verification on every coach, staff member and regular volunteer, renewed annually.
  • Mandated reporter training for all staff, with a written escalation procedure and a named safeguarding lead.
  • Credential-based digital access with time-stamped logging. Minors have facility access only during staffed, supervised hours or with a guardian present.
  • Parent-controlled check-in and check-out with arrival and departure notifications, authorised-pickup control and late-pickup alerts.
  • Supervised waiting zones in direct sight of the front desk, and no unsupervised one-to-one adult contact with a minor anywhere in the building.
  • An independent-majority Academy board with a written conflicts-of-interest policy and annual disclosures.
IF A YOUNG PERSON NEEDS HELP RIGHT NOW

The Academy is not a crisis service. If you or a young person you care about is in distress, free confidential support is available around the clock.

988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline — call or text 988

Crisis Text Line — text HOME to 741741

In an emergency, call 911.

Support The Work

HOW THIS GETS FUNDED

EPIC Life Academy is a 501(c)(3) funded separately from the sports complex through grants, donations and sponsorship. The Academy owns the grant-funded components of the campus outright, which is what keeps youth programming from ever being the first thing cut when a tournament wants the floor.

Sponsors can underwrite a specific program rather than buy signage: a season of youth league fees, the scholarship fund, coach training certification, or the family programming series. Every dollar is reported against outcomes we publish annually.

GET INVOLVED

Coach a season. Underwrite a program. Bring your school or church group. Or tell us what young people in this community need that we haven't thought of.
